deities: Lord Shiva as Sundareswara ('God of Beauty') - main deity
festivals: Arattu Mahotsavam - 8-day (some sources say 10-day) annual festival in Meenam (March-April), with kodiyettam, ezhunnallathu, pallivetta, caparisoned elephants and fireworks; arattu performed at Payyambalam Beach

history.dynasty: None (modern temple; Sri Narayana Guru movement, early 20th century)
history.period: Consecrated 11 April 1916 between 3:00 and 3:20 AM during the ascendancy of the Pooyam (Pushya) star
history.summary: One of two temples in Kannur district consecrated by the saint-philosopher and social reformer Sri Narayana Guru Devan (the other being the Jagannatha Temple at Thalassery). It was built at the instance of the Thiyya community of North Malabar, led by Varathoor Kaniyil Kunhi Kannan, to give the community a spiritual sanctuary for Satvik worship free of the tamasic practices then prevalent; Guru agreed after Kannan met him at Shivagiri and later visited Kannur in 1907. The Talap site was chosen where remnants of an ancient temple were unearthed. Guru named Shiva 'Sundareswara' (God of Beauty) - per one visitor review, on the reasoning that the people and the place are beautiful (weakly sourced - verify). Subsequent additions: Guru's statue, Dwajastambam and Deepastambam (1938), Balikkappura (1939), Gajamandapam (1943) and the temple pond (1946). The traditional Kerala-style complex has a chathura sreekovil, chuttambalam, namaskara mandapam and a huge peepal tree. CSV TOWN NOTE: the temple stands at Talap, a suburb about 2 km from Kannur railway station, within Kannur city - the CSV town 'Kannur' is therefore approximately correct.

name: Sundareswara Temple

town_description: Talap is a suburban locality of Kannur city, about 2 km from Kannur Railway Station and 3 km from the New Bus Stand at Thavakkara. The temple is a city temple within Kannur's urban area.
